speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after a tympanoplasty; can you describe exactly when this pain occurs and how severe it is on a scale of 1 to 10?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Incus Dislocation (Disconnection).

The history of trauma from eating (shooting pain) combined with the specific difficulty wearing earrings suggests a mechanical issue with the ossicular chain, likely a re-disconnection of the incus following your recent tympanoplasty. I need to confirm if there has been any recent loud noise exposure or if the pain is strictly triggered by chewing to rule out other causes.

REQUEST TEST: High-Resolution CT Temporal Bone.
REQUEST IMAGES: Pre-op and Post-op tympanoplasty images.
